features.title: TCP, UDP, and Linux socket semantics
features.current: Unix stream sockets support X11, AF_PACKET exchanges Ethernet, and AF_INET supports raw ICMP/ping and IPv4 UDP datagrams with tested checksums, binding, queues, errors, readiness and retained I/O. Ordinary IPv4 TCP streams add active/passive connections, vector/peek I/O, half-close, nonblocking refusal/readiness and native host client/server transfers on both emulated NICs. TCP MSG_WAITALL retains vector progress across delayed input and descriptor replacement, returns transferred bytes on deadline/signals, and completed detached endpoints use bounded compact TIME-WAIT records; native comparisons and VM cycles exceed the general socket capacity. TCP/Unix accepts reserve output descriptors before waiting; native/VM tests cover full tables, held slots, listener replacement, fork/exec, signals, deadlines and owner release. Bounded NETLINK_ROUTE sockets support tagged IPv4 route control, dumps, complete address updates and retained datagram I/O. Shared Linux receive/send socket timeouts capture finite monotonic I/O deadlines and reclaim retained descriptions on expiry and interruption. Unix datagram descriptors serve interface configuration only. Full TCP retained-call, reclamation and controlled fault acceptance, IPv6 UDP, complete connect interruption/deadline semantics, ancillary data and the complete socket contract remain required. Blocking TCP writes retain progress, imported vectors and entry blocking mode through queue pressure; native/VM comparisons cover replacement, finite deadlines, signals, immediate nonblocking prefixes and exact queued bytes after user-source release. TCP copies check stream state before user pages and commit received bytes only after successful copying; guarded native/VM comparisons cover unavailable buffers, copy faults, short mapped prefixes and exact queued/delivered ownership. TCP pending connect completion is separate from handshake state; failed attempts consume errors and permit same-description reuse while preserving explicit bindings/options and releasing automatic port ownership. Native/VM comparisons cover ordinary completion, descriptor/destination retention, signals/restart, finite deadlines and exact accepted-child ownership. The first controlled NIC loss subset verifies actual active/passive handshake, data and FIN retransmissions, elapsed initial retry clocks, exact bidirectional bytes and wrapped peer sequence space with independent captures and all native/guest profiles; wider controlled-wire acceptance remains required.
